newsitem.title: MEXICO: Low wage growth biggest drag on Mexico GDP -poll.
newsitem.headline: Low wage growth biggest drag on Mexico GDP -poll.

text.p: The slow recovery of real wages is the factor most likely to slow the pace of Mexican growth in the second half of the year, while inflation was not an issue at all, a survey of 29 independent economists showed on Tuesday.
The survey, conducted by the Mexican central bank and obtained by Reuters, also showed that political uncertainty would have scarcely any effect.
Most important was low wage growth, followed by limited availability of funding, conditions in the banking sector and the level of domestic debt.
Increases in wage costs and high inflationary pressures both failed to register at all, while currency appreciation was only represented a moderate drag on growth.
The economists' average forecast for gross domestic product (GDP) was for growth of 5.51 percent in the second quarter of 1997, and for 4.91 percent for the year as a whole.
The maximum Q2 GDP forecast was for 7.00 percent and the minimum was 3.70 percent.
The maximum 1997 GDP forecast was for 5.70 percent while the minimum was 4.00 percent. ((--Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
